content.content:
---
name: releasing-a-cloudflare-site
description: How a site served from Cloudflare is released — the version contract, the guards that stop a release loop or a half-release, forcing one, rolling one back, and which parts of Cloudflare only a person can change. Use when changing the release task, the wrangler config or the analytics loader, and when a release parks.
metadata:
  force-load-on-file-edits-paths:
    - "**/wrangler.json"
    - "**/wrangler.jsonc"
    - "**/tasks/site-release/**"
---

# Releasing a Cloudflare-served site

A release is one thing: the default branch's tree, at a version the release itself cuts,
uploaded to Cloudflare. The `cloudflare-site/site-release` task owns all of it — its
[README](../../tasks/site-release/README.md) says what the worker does; this says how to
operate it and what a change to it must not break.

## The four properties a change preserves

- **The version names what shipped.** `package.json` is the only source and the page stamps
  are generated from it, so the bump and the upload are one run — and the bump goes first,
  because of the two possible drifts only one is invisible: a site serving a version the repo
  has no record of. A number consumed by an upload that then failed is visible in the park and
  costs nothing.
- **A release cannot re-arm itself.** The gate is "the branch has moved past the last release
  commit", read off the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer. Anything that makes the release's own commit
  look like ordinary work releases nightly, forever.
- **Only the published directory is published.** `assets.directory` is the outer boundary, and
  the repo around it holds the vendored mount, the queue's workers and the packs — none of which
  may reach a public URL. Inside it, `.assetsignore` holds back what is documentation rather
  than page, so a file landing there is not automatically a public URL.
- **The beacon token is injected, never committed.** A published loader ships with the
  placeholder and no-ops; the deploy substitutes the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repository
  variable into the copy it uploads. Changing what the page loads or logs changes the promise,
  so the site's own privacy disclosure moves in the same commit.

## Releasing now rather than tonight

The release is the queue's, so force it the way any task is forced:

```
gh workflow run claudinite-scheduler.yml -f wake=cloudflare-site/site-release
```

The gate is still evaluated when the item is picked, so a force with nothing to release rolls
with its reason on record rather than shipping a duplicate.

## Rolling back

Revert on the branch and let the next release carry it — the revert sits above the last release
commit, so the gate opens on it; force the run with the command above when it cannot wait for
the nightly anchor. Don't add a rollback lever: it would be a second path to production, with
its own version arithmetic to keep in step.

## What only a person can change

Everything on the Cloudflare side — the account, the API token and its scopes, and whether the
domain is a zone on that account at all. The wrangler config claims the apex (and usually
`www`) as custom domains, so a deploy fails outright until the zone is there. That is the
intended failure: a release that quietly published to a URL nobody visits is worse than one that
stops and says so. Those steps are the pack's `adoptionHandover`, filed as an issue when the
pack is adopted.

## What the previous host left behind

Adding a zone imports the records the old host was serving, and a custom domain cannot be
attached over an existing `CNAME` — so an inherited `www` record blocks the deploy, and old
apex records keep serving the old host until they go. Nobody is asked to check for these: the
release resolves each claimed hostname in public DNS before it consumes a version number and
parks naming the record it found ([preflight.mjs](../../tasks/site-release/preflight.mjs)), and
`no-second-publisher` catches the repo-side leftovers — a workflow that still deploys, a `CNAME`
file still claiming the domain for GitHub Pages. An unreachable resolver is inconclusive, not a
verdict: the release proceeds and says the probe did not run.

## Reading a park

The worker names the lane it wants, so the label is the diagnosis. **`action`** is a credential,
a scope, the zone, or an inherited record, and the comment names which — nothing is wrong with
the code. **`decision`** means a surface the release depends on changed underneath it (no
`package.json` on the branch, no `assets.directory`, the analytics placeholder gone), and
whether the release should follow is a person's call. **`failure`** means read the trace; that
lane also holds the next occurrence until the item is woken or closed, so a broken release stops
rather than filing a queue of items that break the same way. A park after the push but before
the upload has consumed a version number — re-queue the item, and the retry counts from the
branch's new tip.

## Changing the release

# Releasing a Cloudflare-served site

A release is one thing: the default branch's tree, at a version the release itself cuts,
uploaded to Cloudflare. The `cloudflare-site/site-release` task owns all of it — its
[README](../../tasks/site-release/README.md) says what the worker does; this says how to
operate it and what a change to it must not break.

## The four properties a change preserves

- **The version names what shipped.** `package.json` is the only source and the page stamps
  are generated from it, so the bump and the upload are one run — and the bump goes first,
  because of the two possible drifts only one is invisible: a site serving a version the repo
  has no record of. A number consumed by an upload that then failed is visible in the park and
  costs nothing.
- **A release cannot re-arm itself.** The gate is "the branch has moved past the last release
  commit", read off the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer. Anything that makes the release's own commit
  look like ordinary work releases nightly, forever.
- **Only the published directory is published.** `assets.directory` is the outer boundary, and
  the repo around it holds the vendored mount, the queue's workers and the packs — none of which
  may reach a public URL. Inside it, `.assetsignore` holds back what is documentation rather
  than page, so a file landing there is not automatically a public URL.
- **The beacon token is injected, never committed.** A published loader ships with the
  placeholder and no-ops; the deploy substitutes the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repository
  variable into the copy it uploads. Changing what the page loads or logs changes the promise,
  so the site's own privacy disclosure moves in the same commit.

## Releasing now rather than tonight

The release is the queue's, so force it the way any task is forced:

```
gh workflow run claudinite-scheduler.yml -f wake=cloudflare-site/site-release
```

The gate is still evaluated when the item is picked, so a force with nothing to release rolls
with its reason on record rather than shipping a duplicate.

## Rolling back

Revert on the branch and let the next release carry it — the revert sits above the last release
commit, so the gate opens on it; force the run with the command above when it cannot wait for
the nightly anchor. Don't add a rollback lever: it would be a second path to production, with
its own version arithmetic to keep in step.

## What only a person can change

Everything on the Cloudflare side — the account, the API token and its scopes, and whether the
domain is a zone on that account at all. The wrangler config claims the apex (and usually
`www`) as custom domains, so a deploy fails outright until the zone is there. That is the
intended failure: a release that quietly published to a URL nobody visits is worse than one that
stops and says so. Those steps are the pack's `adoptionHandover`, filed as an issue when the
pack is adopted.

## What the previous host left behind

Adding a zone imports the records the old host was serving, and a custom domain cannot be
attached over an existing `CNAME` — so an inherited `www` record blocks the deploy, and old
apex records keep serving the old host until they go. Nobody is asked to check for these: the
release resolves each claimed hostname in public DNS before it consumes a version number and
parks naming the record it found ([preflight.mjs](../../tasks/site-release/preflight.mjs)), and
`no-second-publisher` catches the repo-side leftovers — a workflow that still deploys, a `CNAME`
file still claiming the domain for GitHub Pages. An unreachable resolver is inconclusive, not a
verdict: the release proceeds and says the probe did not run.

## Reading a park

The worker names the lane it wants, so the label is the diagnosis. **`action`** is a credential,
a scope, the zone, or an inherited record, and the comment names which — nothing is wrong with
the code. **`decision`** means a surface the release depends on changed underneath it (no
`package.json` on the branch, no `assets.directory`, the analytics placeholder gone), and
whether the release should follow is a person's call. **`failure`** means read the trace; that
lane also holds the next occurrence until the item is woken or closed, so a broken release stops
rather than filing a queue of items that break the same way. A park after the push but before
the upload has consumed a version number — re-queue the item, and the retry counts from the
branch's new tip.

## Changing the release

- **Never add a workflow that publishes.** The release lives in code-work precisely because
  `wrangler` is a CLI and needs no `uses:` step; a workflow beside it would bypass both the
  version bump and the queue's failure lane. `no-second-publisher` refuses one, so don't also
  guard it in review.
- **Keep `wrangler` pinned to an exact version**, so two nights cannot run different toolchains
  without a commit saying so.
- **Correct the task README and this file in the same commit** as any behaviour change — a
  description that still says the old thing is worse than none.

content.content:
# site-release — what the worker does

Publishes the site tree to Cloudflare and records the version that went out. There is
no `task.md` because there is no agent: a release is a version number, a push and an
upload, and none of the three is a judgment call.

The operating knowledge — how to force one, how to roll one back, what is on the
Cloudflare side and what a park means — is the
[releasing-a-cloudflare-site](../../skills/releasing-a-cloudflare-site/SKILL.md)
skill. This file is only what the worker does.

## The run

1. **Ask public DNS what the claimed hostnames answer.** [`preflight.mjs`](preflight.mjs)
   says why this runs before a version is consumed and what it can and cannot see.
2. **Read the branch tip.** The version is computed from `package.json` as the remote
   has it, never from the executor's checkout, so a release cannot advance from a
   stale number; the published tree and the claimed hostnames come from the wrangler
   config at that same commit.
3. **Advance and stamp.** [`bump-version.mjs`](../../bump-version.mjs) owns the scheme
   and the page stamp; the worker imports its two pure functions rather than shelling
   out, because it is stamping a commit it is building, not a working tree.
4. **Push the bump to the default branch**, rebuilding on whatever landed underneath
   and retrying — the scheduler and the maintenance PRs land there too, and a lost
   race would leave the repo naming an older version than the one being served.
5. **Check out that exact commit** and substitute the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon
   token into the copy about to be uploaded. The token is public and lives in the
   `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repository variable; with no variable set the
   placeholder ships and the loader no-ops, which the run says out loud either way.
6. **`wrangler deploy`**, run from the directory holding the wrangler config, then
   fetch each claimed hostname and report what it answered.

The bump lands **before** the upload on purpose. Both halves can fail, and only one
of the two drifts is silent: a site serving a version the repo has no record of. A
version number consumed by a release that then failed to upload is visible in the
park and costs nothing — the next release takes the next number.

## Why the declaration reads as it does

**No workflow.** A Pages deploy has to be one: its publish steps are marketplace
actions, and no task can invoke a `uses:` step. `wrangler` is a CLI, so the whole
release fits in code-work and the trigger, the gate and the failure lane come from
the queue instead of from YAML.

**`unreleased-commits`** ([`preconditions.mjs`](preconditions.mjs)) is the task's own
term because no built-in asks a release's question. The file says why the two nearest
built-ins are both wrong here.

**`on_interrupt: needs-human`** because a release is a one-shot external effect: a
reclaimed claim must not re-run it, spend a second version number and re-upload.

**`code_work_required_secrets`** names the two Cloudflare credentials so a repo that
has not configured them parks saying *which* one is missing, rather than failing
somewhere inside `wrangler`.

**`expected_outcome: no_code_changes`** — the run opens no pull request. It does
commit, but to the default branch directly: a version bump reviewed after the fact is
a review of a number a machine derived, and holding the release for it would mean the
site lags the repo by however long the PR sits.

**Daily.** A release goes out the night after anything lands, and a night with
nothing to release files no run at all.
=== task.json ===
{
  "$schema": "../../../claudinite-tasks/task.schema.json",
  "id": "site-release",
  "description": "Cuts the next site version, stamps it into the published pages and uploads the site tree to Cloudflare so the claimed domain serves what the default branch says. The bump lands on the branch before the upload, so the repo never records a release that did not go out.",
  "trigger": "schedule",
  "preconditions": [
    "due:daily",
    "unreleased-commits"
  ],
  "expected_outcome": "no_code_changes",
  "on_interrupt": "needs-human",
  "code_work": "node worker.mjs",
  "code_work_timeout": 900,
  "code_work_required_secrets": [
    "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN",
    "CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID"
  ],
  "agent_model": "none"
}

=== build-site.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The site's build step — everything that must happen to the tree before the
# publish set is assembled. Named by `build_command` in .github/site.config, so
# the release pipeline and the pull-request gate run exactly this, and a change
# here is exercised on the PR before it can reach a deploy.
#
# These were two inline steps of the hand-rolled pages.yml the static-website
# pack replaces; the logic is unchanged and it produces the same two files.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# The build stamp the debug pill shows: the last commit's time, in the timezone
# the festival is followed from, so "when was this built" reads the way a user
# expects rather than in UTC.
TIME=$(TZ='Asia/Jerusalem' git log -1 --date=format-local:'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' --format=%cd)
printf 'window.__BUILD__ = { time: "%s" };\n' "$TIME" > js/build-info.js
echo "Stamped build time $TIME (Israel) into js/build-info.js"

# The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token, declared in site.config's build_vars
# and exported into this script's environment by the pipeline.
#
# On the pipeline the else-branch is unreachable: a declared build_var with no
# value fails the run before the build starts, precisely so a deploy can never
# publish a page whose beacon is silently dead. The branch is here for the OTHER
# caller — a local run or a fork, where the variable legitimately does not exist
# and leaving the placeholder in place (analytics no-ops) is the right outcome.
if [ -n "${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  sed -i "s#REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN#${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN}#" js/analytics.js
  echo "Injected the Cloudflare Web Analytics token from CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN."
else
  echo "CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN is not set (local run or fork) — analytics stays off, placeholder retained."
fi

=== verify.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The repo's single verification gate: unit tests, JavaScript parse-checks,
# Python byte-compilation, and the Claudinite conformance sweep. Both the
# pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit) and the pipeline's PR gate
# (.github/workflows/static-site-ci.yml, which runs it as the test_command named
# in .github/site.config) run *this* script.
#
# The conformance sweep is here because it was the one CI step this script did
# not cover, and the gap was not theoretical: a commit that passed `npm run
# verify` went red on GitHub for a blocking `claudinite-isolation` finding, and
# cost an extra round trip to notice and a third commit to fix. A gate you can
# pass and still break CI is not a gate. It is the slowest step by an order of
# magnitude, so it runs last — a syntax error should still fail in a second.
#
# CI runs the sweep again in its own earlier step (that workflow is vendored
# from the static-website pack and re-vendored on refresh, so it is not ours to
# trim). The duplicate costs CI ~9s and buys separate attribution there; the
# point of this copy is the pre-commit and local path, where nothing ran it.
#
# Still NOT the whole of CI: `npm run test:ui` (the ui-requirements job),
# scripts/build-site.sh and the assemble-site dry run are outside this script.
# Green here means the fast lanes are green, not that GitHub will be.
#
# A few seconds and dependency-free — everything uses the node / python already
# needed to work on the project.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

step() { printf '\n\033[1m▶ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }

step "Unit tests — node --test"
# The shared/ helpers both front-ends import, the Now page's own js/ tests, the
# planner's own tests, plus the local packs' — one glob for each pack's own
# pack.test.mjs (its checks' red-first fixtures), one for the shared task
# declaration test, one for the per-task tests beside each task. Those tests import
# every pack manifest and task declaration, so they are also what parse-checks that
# tree (the syntax sweep below deliberately stays off the .claudinite mount).
# Keep in step with the "test" script in package.json.
# product/requirements/ contributes its default-lane gates here: the coverage
# bijection, the gallery gate, and the pure logic cases. The browser-driven
# screen/behavior lanes are `npm run test:ui` (CI's ui-requirements job), not
# this fast path.
node --test shared/__tests__/*.test.mjs js/__tests__/*.test.mjs plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs plan2/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs product/requirements/*.test.js product/requirements/logic/logic.test.js .claudinite/local/packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/tasks/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/tasks/*/*.test.mjs

step "JavaScript syntax — node --check"
# Only our own tracked source: the js/ app, the plan/ planner, the shared/
# code both import, and the scripts/ tooling. Never the vendored .claudinite
# mount (not our code) or the plan/design/ mock (HTML).
js_files=$(git ls-files 'js' 'plan' 'plan2' 'planJerusalem' 'scripts' 'shared' 'product' 'design-concepts' | { grep -E '\.m?js$' || true; } | { grep -v '^plan/design/' || true; })
# `node --check` takes one file per process, and ~170 sequential node startups
# was the bulk of this script's runtime (4.5s of 7s). xargs -P fans them across
# the cores instead; -n 1 because the flag genuinely accepts only one path.
# xargs exits 123 if any invocation failed, which `set -e` turns into a failure.
if [ -n "$js_files" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$js_files" | xargs -P "$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 4)" -n 1 node --check
  echo "checked $(printf '%s\n' "$js_files" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') JavaScript file(s)"
else
  echo "no JavaScript sources found — skipping"
fi

step "Python syntax — py_compile"
py_files=$(git ls-files 'scraper/*.py')
if [ -z "$py_files" ]; then
  echo "no Python sources found — skipping"
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  python3 -m py_compile $py_files
  echo "checked $(printf '%s\n' $py_files | wc -l | tr -d ' ') Python file(s)"
else
  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
fi

step "Normalizer self-test — normalize.py --selftest"
# Exercises the raw→master→day-file→shows.min.json transforms on a fixture (no
# network / no raw data), so the packer and the day-file builder are covered here
# and the round-trip decoder is covered by plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest
else
  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
fi

step "Jerusalem parse self-test — jerusalem/parse.py"
# The Jerusalem scrape is one-shot and its fetch half can only be checked against
# the live site; its Hebrew parsing half runs offline on markup shaped like the
# source's, which makes it the only verification that change can get here — so it
# is wired in rather than left to be remembered.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 scraper/jerusalem/parse.py
else
  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
fi

step "Claudinite conformance — check_the_world.mjs"
# The same command CI's "Conformance sweep" step runs. World scope: the rules
# that audit repo state as it is now (the work-scope half runs from the Stop
# hook). Blocking findings exit non-zero and fail this script; advisories print
# and pass. `--root .` rather than letting it fall back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR,
# so the sweep always covers the tree this script already cd'd into.
#
# Naming a path inside the mount is the one thing claudinite-isolation forbids
# outside the wiring files; it is excused by name in .claudinite-checks.json's
# `accept` list, with the reason, rather than left to slip through the rule's
# unquoted-path blind spot.
node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --root .

printf '\n\033[32m✓ all checks passed\033[0m\n'

content.content:
name: Assemble the published site
description: >-
  Builds the Pages artifact directory from the repo's EXPLICIT publish set —
  `publish_paths` under `publish_root`, and nothing else. The artifact is
  composed from a named list rather than "the repo minus the dirs we know to
  hide": a subtractive rule publishes every file nobody thought to exclude (a
  draft, a scratch note, an agent-tooling dir, a key), and it publishes each new
  one silently the day it lands. An additive list can only ever publish what the
  repo asked for, and its failure mode — a file that does not show up — is
  visible on the site.

  Two loud guards, because a Pages deploy has no other reviewer: a publish path
  that does not exist fails the run (a rename that silently dropped a directory
  from the site is exactly what the explicit list is for), and so does an
  assembled site with no index.html at its root (a site whose "/" 404s is a
  broken deploy, not a deploy).

  Composite so it adds no reusable-workflow nesting level, and used by both the
  Pages deploy and PR CI, so a PR proves its publish set assembles before it can
  break the live site.

inputs:
  publish_root:
    description: Directory the site is rooted at ("." = repo root)
    required: true
  publish_paths:
    description: Space-separated publish set, relative to publish_root
    required: true
  dest:
    description: Directory to assemble into, relative to the workspace
    required: false
    default: _site

outputs:
  dest:
    description: The assembled site directory (workspace-relative)
    value: ${{ inputs.dest }}

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - shell: bash
      env:
        PUBLISH_ROOT: ${{ inputs.publish_root }}
        # Intentionally word-split below into the individual publish paths.
        PUBLISH_PATHS: ${{ inputs.publish_paths }}
        DEST: ${{ inputs.dest }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        dest="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$DEST"
        rm -rf "$dest"
        mkdir -p "$dest"
        cd "$PUBLISH_ROOT"
        for p in $PUBLISH_PATHS; do
          if [ ! -e "$p" ]; then
            echo "::error::publish path '$p' does not exist under '$PUBLISH_ROOT' — fix .github/site.config or restore the file" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "$dest/$(dirname "$p")"
          cp -R "$p" "$dest/$(dirname "$p")/"

shell: bash

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The PR's real head, not the synthetic merge commit, so CI evaluates
          # what the session's own Stop hook does.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - name: Conformance sweep
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs

      - name: Run the repo's gate
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.test_command != ''
        run: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.test_command }}

      # Repo variables the config declares, exported into the build's env.
      # `vars` structurally cannot carry a secret, which is the point: this
      # feeds the step that produces the published artifact.
      - name: Export the declared build variables
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.build_vars != ''
        env:
          DECLARED_BUILD_VARS: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.build_vars }}
          REPO_VARS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
        run: node .github/actions/read-site-config/export-build-vars.mjs

      - name: Build the site
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.build_command != ''
        run: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.build_command }}

      # Assemble into a scratch dir (not _site) so nothing here can be mistaken
      # for a deployable artifact; the guards — every publish path exists, the
      # site has an index.html — are the point.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assemble-site
        with:
          publish_root: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.publish_root }}
          publish_paths: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.publish_paths }}
          dest: _site-check

input.title: Move the published site into site/ (step 1 of the Cloudflare migration)
input.body:
The owner's ask: *"Let's move from github pages to deploy to Cloudflare. Adopt the relevant package and lets go."* — then, on being shown what the pack forces: *"Move to `site`. Make this a first PR without changing anything else. Then we merge, deploy, check and continue the migration to cloudflare."*

## Why this step exists

The `cloudflare-site` canon pack publishes exactly one directory — `assets.directory` in a
`wrangler.json` — and its `publishes-a-site-directory` check **blocks** pointing that at the repo
root, because the root holds the vendored Claudinite mount, the queue workers, `scraper/` and the
~10 MB of pipeline inputs under `data/`. The release task has **no build step**: it uploads the
committed tree verbatim (after substituting the analytics beacon token). So the published tree has
to exist in the repo as a directory.

This repo's site lives at the root. Reshaping it is the large, risky half of the migration — it
moves 106 tracked files, the scraper's output paths, the UI-requirements harness root and four of
this repo's own checks. Doing it **while still on GitHub Pages** means the reshape can be proved
against the live site before the host changes underneath it.

## Scope of this issue (PR 1)

Move only. The site keeps deploying to GitHub Pages, at the same URLs.

- [ ] `git mv` the publish set into `site/` — the four pages, the favicons, `.nojekyll`, `css/`,
      `js/`, `shared/`, `plan/`, `plan2/`, `planJerusalem/`, and the *published* data into
      `site/data/`. Every fetch in the product is page-relative, so no URL and no fetch path changes.
- [ ] `data/` at the root keeps only the pipeline inputs (`data/normalized/shows.json`,
      `data/prices.json`) and the raw caches; `scraper/normalize.py` and friends write their
      published artifacts into `site/data/`.
- [ ] `.github/site.config`: `publish_root=site`, so the Pages artifact root is the site — the live
      URLs gain no `/site/` prefix.
- [ ] `scripts/build-site.sh`, `scripts/verify.sh`, the UI harness's served root, and the four local
      checks that hardcode `data/`, `plan/package.json` and verify.sh's source-dir list.
- [ ] `npm run verify` and `npm run test:ui` green; goldens unchanged (the pages' bytes don't move).

## Explicitly NOT in this step

No `wrangler.json`, no pack declaration change, no workflow deletions. GitHub Pages stays the
publisher until the reshape is proved live.

## The rest of the migration (later PRs, after this one is merged and checked)

2. Adopt `cloudflare-site`, undeclare `static-website`, add `wrangler.json` claiming
   `edfringenow.com` + `www.edfringenow.com`, retire the five `static-site-*` workflows and
   `.github/site.config`, author the repo's own PR CI gate (no canon pack owns generic CI), and move
   the version pill onto the pack's generated `title="version …"` stamp.
3. The Cloudflare account steps, which are the pack's `adoptionHandover` and only a person can do:
   add the zone and move the registrar's nameservers, then set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
   `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` as repository secrets. Filed as its own handover issue when step 2 lands.

Moving the nameservers is world-reaching and affects every record on the domain, not just the site
— it is the owner's action and its own gate.

lines: -  <meta name="description" content="How EdFringeNow works with keyboards, screen readers and reduced motion — and how to tell us when it doesn't." />

-

We want EdFringeNow to be usable by everyone — on a phone, on a street, in a hurry.

-
  • Full keyboard navigation, with a clearly visible focus outline on every control.

-
  • Semantic markup and ARIA labels, so a screen reader can announce the plan, the filters, and the list of shows.

-
  • Respects your device's “reduce motion” setting — animations switch off when you ask them to.

-
  • Large tap targets and a single, legible column that scales down to small screens.

-

We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. We're a small project and we won't always hit it perfectly.

-

If anything is hard to use with your assistive technology, please tell us at support@edfringenow.com — say what you were trying to do and what got in the way, and we'll fix it.
-  <meta name="description" content="EdFringeNow counts visits with privacy-first, cookieless analytics — no cookies, no personal data, no cross-site tracking. Here's exactly what's measured." />

-

The short version: we count visits using privacy-first, cookieless analytics. No cookies, no personal data, no ads, and no following you around the web.

-

To understand roughly how many people use EdFringeNow, we use Cloudflare Web Analytics — a privacy-first tool chosen precisely because it doesn't use cookies, doesn't store personal data, and can't identify you or follow you to other sites. It records anonymous, aggregate signals only: page views, the referring site, and a broad region worked out from your request (your IP address is used to derive that, but is never stored).

-

So this site is not analytics-free, and we would rather say so plainly than imply otherwise: we do count visits. What we don't do is build a picture of you. There is no cross-site tracking and no advertising profile — which is also why there's no cookie-consent banner to click through.

-

We don't sell your data, and we don't track you across the web. No ads. No advertising trackers. No cookies set by us. No accounts and no sign-up.

-

EdFringeNow is a static website. It runs entirely in your browser, with no server of ours behind it — so beyond the anonymous, aggregate analytics described above, there is nothing about you for us to log or keep.

-

If you allow location access, your position is used only in your browser to work out which shows are near you. It is never sent to us or to anyone else. Deny it and the app simply falls back to central Edinburgh — everything still works.

-

Like any web page, opening EdFringeNow fetches a few files from other services. Those services see your IP address and browser as part of a normal web request, the same as visiting any website:

-
  • The map library (unpkg) and typefaces (Google Fonts) from their content delivery networks.

-
  • The privacy-first analytics beacon (a small script) from Cloudflare.

-

The show and venue listings are plain files served from this site. They describe the festival, not you.

-

“Open in Maps” opens Google Maps, and ticket links open edfringe.com. Once you follow a link, that site's own privacy policy applies — not this one.
-  <meta name="description" content="EdFringeNow is a free, independent tool for catching a Fringe show right now. The short terms." />

-

EdFringeNow is a free tool to help you catch an Edinburgh Fringe show right now. Using it means agreeing to the following — kept deliberately short.

-

We offer EdFringeNow in good faith but make no guarantees. Show times, durations, prices, availability, walking times, and “you'll make it” estimates can be wrong or out of date. Check the venue or edfringe.com before you rely on anything — especially before buying a ticket or dashing across town.

-

EdFringeNow is an independent project by Missing Bulb. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe Society or edfringe.com. Ticket links send you to edfringe.com, where their terms apply.

-

Maps come from OpenStreetMap and Google Maps; tickets from edfringe.com. Your use of those services is governed by their own terms.

-

To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for anything arising from your use of the site — including a missed show, train, or dinner. Use your own judgement.
-  <!-- A map pin whose head is a clock face: "a show near you, starting now". -->

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Normalize scraped edfringe show data into website-ready JSON.

Reads the raw scrape (events + venues + genres produced by fetch_shows.py) and
emits the site's data layers:

  data/normalized/shows.json   master, normalized, one record per show with all
                               its performances. The source of truth for later
                               processing / regenerating the day files. NOT sent
                               to the browser.

  data/normalized/shows.min.json
                               the compact wire form of the master, and the file
                               the planner actually downloads. Losslessly packed
                               against the venues.json lookups: every enum (genre,
                               room, subgenre, age restriction) is an index into a
                               shared list; venueName is rebuilt from the venue
                               code + room; smallImage is dropped when it equals
                               image; booleans are 1/0; dates are an MMDD int;
                               field names are 1-3 chars. The planner rehydrates it
                               with venues.json + the availability sidecar below
                               (see plan/plan.js). Deliberately carries NOTHING
                               that changes through the day, so an unchanged
                               festival regenerates it byte-for-byte and a client
                               can hold it for days.

  data/normalized/availability.min.json
                               per-performance ticket status, split OUT of the
                               catalogue above precisely because it is the one
                               thing that moves during the festival. Self-contained
                               (it carries its own status list and indexes into
                               nothing), so the ticket refresh rewrites this file
                               alone and every other artifact stays untouched —
                               a returning visitor re-downloads availability,
                               not the whole catalogue.

  data/normalized/descriptions.min.json
                               slug -> full show description, as a sidecar the
                               planner fetches SEPARATELY and lazily. It exists
                               so the catalogue above stays small enough to block
                               on: descriptions are the bulkiest field and are
                               needed by nothing on first paint — only by the
                               hover card and by search, both of which work
                               (from the 160-char `blurb` in the catalogue) and
                               simply reach further once this lands.

  data/venues.json             shared lookup, sent once:
                               {venues, rooms, genres, subgenres, ticketStatuses,
                               ageRestrictions}. `venues` is keyed by venue code
                               ("venue number") -> name, address, postcode, lat,
                               lng; the rest are the global de-duplicated string
                               lists the day files and shows.min.json index into.

  data/days/2026-08-DD.json    one file per August FRINGE day, holding only the
                               shows performing that day with the minimum a card
                               needs. A fringe day runs 06:00 → 06:00 (see
                               FRINGE_DAY_START), so the file also carries the
                               small hours of the next morning, written with an
                               extended start time ("24:30" for 00:30).
                               Normalized: venue is referenced by code and
                               genre/room by index into the global rooms/genres
                               lists (all in venues.json). This is what the site
                               loads on open.
  data/days/index.json         list of available days + per-day counts.

Locations are normalized to a venue code plus the specific room (space) of the
show. Venue coordinates are geocoded from UK postcodes via postcodes.io and
cached in venues.json so a refresh only geocodes new venues.

Times are normalized the same way, and it matters just as much: the API stamps

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	#
3	# The repo's single verification gate: unit tests, JavaScript parse-checks,
4	# Python byte-compilation, and the Claudinite conformance sweep. Both the
5	# pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit) and the pipeline's PR gate
6	# (.github/workflows/static-site-ci.yml, which runs it as the test_command named
7	# in .github/site.config) run *this* script.
8	#
9	# The conformance sweep is here because it was the one CI step this script did
10	# not cover, and the gap was not theoretical: a commit that passed `npm run
11	# verify` went red on GitHub for a blocking `claudinite-isolation` finding, and
12	# cost an extra round trip to notice and a third commit to fix. A gate you can
13	# pass and still break CI is not a gate. It is the slowest step by an order of
14	# magnitude, so it runs last — a syntax error should still fail in a second.
15	#
16	# CI runs the sweep again in its own earlier step (that workflow is vendored
17	# from the static-website pack and re-vendored on refresh, so it is not ours to
18	# trim). The duplicate costs CI ~9s and buys separate attribution there; the
19	# point of this copy is the pre-commit and local path, where nothing ran it.
20	#
21	# Still NOT the whole of CI: `npm run test:ui` (the ui-requirements job),
22	# scripts/build-site.sh and the assemble-site dry run are outside this script.
23	# Green here means the fast lanes are green, not that GitHub will be.
24	#
25	# A few seconds and dependency-free — everything uses the node / python already
26	# needed to work on the project.
27	set -euo pipefail
28	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
29	
30	step() { printf '\n\033[1m▶ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
31	
32	step "Unit tests — node --test"
33	# The shared/ helpers both front-ends import, the Now page's own js/ tests, the
34	# planner's own tests, plus the local packs' — one glob for each pack's own
35	# pack.test.mjs (its checks' red-first fixtures), one for the shared task
36	# declaration test, one for the per-task tests beside each task. Those tests import
37	# every pack manifest and task declaration, so they are also what parse-checks that
38	# tree (the syntax sweep below deliberately stays off the .claudinite mount).
39	# Keep in step with the "test" script in package.json.
40	# product/requirements/ contributes its default-lane gates here: the coverage
41	# bijection, the gallery gate, and the pure logic cases. The browser-driven
42	# screen/behavior lanes are `npm run test:ui` (CI's ui-requirements job), not
43	# this fast path.
44	node --test site/shared/__tests__/*.test.mjs site/js/__tests__/*.test.mjs site/plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs site/plan2/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs product/requirements/*.test.js product/requirements/logic/logic.test.js .claudinite/local/packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/tasks/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/tasks/*/*.test.mjs
45	
46	step "JavaScript syntax — node --check"
47	# Only our own tracked source: everything the site ships (site/), the scripts/
48	# tooling, the requirements harness and the design concepts. Never the vendored
49	# .claudinite mount (not our code) or the plan/design/ mock (HTML).
50	js_files=$(git ls-files 'site' 'scripts' 'product' 'design-concepts' | { grep -E '\.m?js$' || true; } | { grep -v '^site/plan/design/' || true; })
51	# `node --check` takes one file per process, and ~170 sequential node startups
52	# was the bulk of this script's runtime (4.5s of 7s). xargs -P fans them across
53	# the cores instead; -n 1 because the flag genuinely accepts only one path.
54	# xargs exits 123 if any invocation failed, which `set -e` turns into a failure.
55	if [ -n "$js_files" ]; then
56	  printf '%s\n' "$js_files" | xargs -P "$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 4)" -n 1 node --check
57	  echo "checked $(printf '%s\n' "$js_files" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') JavaScript file(s)"
58	else
59	  echo "no JavaScript sources found — skipping"
60	fi
61	
62	step "Python syntax — py_compile"
63	py_files=$(git ls-files 'scraper/*.py')
64	if [ -z "$py_files" ]; then
65	  echo "no Python sources found — skipping"
66	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
67	  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
68	  python3 -m py_compile $py_files
69	  echo "checked $(printf '%s\n' $py_files | wc -l | tr -d ' ') Python file(s)"
70	else
71	  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
72	fi
73	
74	step "Normalizer self-test — normalize.py --selftest"
75	# Exercises the raw→master→day-file→shows.min.json transforms on a fixture (no
76	# network / no raw data), so the packer and the day-file builder are covered here
77	# and the round-trip decoder is covered by plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs.
78	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
79	  python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest
80	else
81	  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
82	fi
83	
84	step "Jerusalem parse self-test — jerusalem/parse.py"
85	# The Jerusalem scrape is one-shot and its fetch half can only be checked against
86	# the live site; its Hebrew parsing half runs offline on markup shaped like the
87	# source's, which makes it the only verification that change can get here — so it
88	# is wired in rather than left to be remembered.
89	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
90	  python3 scraper/jerusalem/parse.py
91	else
92	  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
93	fi
94	
95	step "Claudinite conformance — check_the_world.mjs"
96	# The same command CI's "Conformance sweep" step runs. World scope: the rules
97	# that audit repo state as it is now (the work-scope half runs from the Stop
98	# hook). Blocking findings exit non-zero and fail this script; advisories print
99	# and pass. `--root .` rather than letting it fall back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR,
100	# so the sweep always covers the tree this script already cd'd into.
101	#
102	# Naming a path inside the mount is the one thing claudinite-isolation forbids
103	# outside the wiring files; it is excused by name in .claudinite-checks.json's
104	# `accept` list, with the reason, rather than left to slip through the rule's
105	# unquoted-path blind spot.
106	node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --root .
107	
108	printf '\n\033[32m✓ all checks passed\033[0m\n'

sed -i 's#the round-trip decoder is covered by plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs.#the round-trip decoder is covered by site/plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs.#' scripts/verify.sh && cat > .github/site.config <<'EOF'
# The static-website pack's keys — every repo-specific value the vendored release
# pipeline reads. Explicit on purpose: nothing here is published, versioned,
# built or tested except what this file names.
#
# The site is its own directory. Everything under site/ IS the site and nothing
# else is: the scraper, the pipeline's working data, docs/, design-concepts/,
# product/, product-wiki/, scripts/ and the agent tooling all live outside it.
# `publish_root=site` makes that directory the artifact's root, so the live URLs
# are unchanged by the move — the site is served from "/" exactly as before.
publish_root=site

# Relative to publish_root. The code DIRECTORIES are named as directories, not
# file by file, and that is a considered trade: a file-by-file list is exact but
# silently breaks the site the day someone adds js/foo.js and forgets this file,
# while a directory keeps working. The cost is that js/__tests__,
# shared/__tests__ and plan/lib/__tests__ ride along — a few KB of harmless test
# code on a public site, which is the cheaper of the two failures.
#
# `data` is now a plain directory entry too. It used to be named file by file to
# hold back the two scraper inputs that no page fetches; those stay behind at the
# repo's own data/, so what remains under site/data is exactly the wire files the
# browser asks for and the list has nothing left to exclude.
#
# plan/ is still enumerated, because plan/design/ is a static mock that is not
# part of the product.
publish_paths=.nojekyll index.html accessibility.html privacy.html terms.html favicon.ico favicon.svg apple-touch-icon.png css js shared package.json plan/index.html plan/plan.css plan/plan.js plan/lib plan2 planJerusalem data

# package.json is the single source of truth; the debug pill fetches it to show
# the running version, which is why it is in the publish set above too. The repo's
# own package.json is at the root, outside the published tree, so the build copies
# it in rather than the repo carrying a second one to drift.
version_files=package.json

# Stamps js/build-info.js, copies the version in, and injects the analytics
# beacon token — the steps that turn the tracked tree into the published one.
# Runs on every pull request as well as on a deploy.
build_command=bash scripts/build-site.sh

# The repo's own gate: unit tests, JS/Python syntax, the normalizer self-test.
# The same script the pre-commit hook runs.
test_command=bash scripts/verify.sh

# The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token. Public by nature — it ships to every
# visitor in the page — so it is a repo VARIABLE, never a secret, which is also
# the only kind of value the pipeline will export into a build.
build_vars=CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN
EOF
echo "site.config rewritten"

build-site.sh updated
# The build stamp the debug pill shows: the last commit's time, in the timezone
# the festival is followed from, so "when was this built" reads the way a user
# expects rather than in UTC.
TIME=$(TZ='Asia/Jerusalem' git log -1 --date=format-local:'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' --format=%cd)
printf 'window.__BUILD__ = { time: "%s" };\n' "$TIME" > site/js/build-info.js
echo "Stamped build time $TIME (Israel) into site/js/build-info.js"

# The version the debug pill and the footer tooltip show. package.json is the
# single source of truth and lives at the repo root, outside the published tree,
# so the published copy is generated here rather than committed — a second
# tracked copy is a number that drifts the first time only one of them is bumped.
cp package.json site/package.json
echo "Copied package.json into the published tree as site/package.json"

# The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token, declared in site.config's build_vars
# and exported into this script's environment by the pipeline.
#
# On the pipeline the else-branch is unreachable: a declared build_var with no
# value fails the run before the build starts, precisely so a deploy can never
# publish a page whose beacon is silently dead. The branch is here for the OTHER
# caller — a local run or a fork, where the variable legitimately does not exist
# and leaving the placeholder in place (analytics no-ops) is the right outcome.
if [ -n "${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  sed -i "s#REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN#${CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN}#" site/js/analytics.js
  echo "Injected the Cloudflare Web Analytics token from CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN."
else
  echo "CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN is not set (local run or fork) — analytics stays off, placeholder retained."
fi

1	// Dependency-free by design: a local pack's checks must load without the
2	// vendored mount, so this returns plain finding objects rather than importing
3	// engine/checks/helpers/findings.mjs.
4	
5	// The repo holds two data trees and normalize.py writes both: `site/data/`, the
6	// wire files the browser fetches, and `data/`, the pipeline's own working files.
7	// Its module header is the authoritative list:
8	//
9	//   site/data/normalized/shows.min.json, availability.min.json, descriptions.min.json
10	//   site/data/venues.json
11	//   site/data/days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json + site/data/days/index.json
12	//   data/normalized/shows.json                   the master, which no page fetches
13	//
14	// Both trees are scanned, because the hazard is the same on either side of the
15	// publish boundary — worse on the published one, where an unowned file is served
16	// to visitors. So a file under either that isn't one of those shapes came from a hand, a
17	// throwaway probe, or a force-added raw cache — and the next `refresh-shows`
18	// run neither maintains it nor knows about it. The patterns are deliberately
19	// shape-based (a dir plus a `.json` leaf) rather than a literal file list, so a
20	// new day file or a new normalized artefact doesn't trip the check; a whole new
21	// output *directory* does, which is the moment a human should confirm the
22	// producer really writes it.
23	const ALLOWED_PATTERNS = [
24	  /^site\/data\/normalized\/[^/]+\.json$/,
25	  /^site\/data\/days\/[^/]+\.json$/,
26	  /^data\/normalized\/[^/]+\.json$/,
27	];
28	
29	// The two roots a committed data file may sit under. Named once so the scan, the
30	// findings and this file's own prose cannot drift apart.
31	const DATA_ROOTS = ['site/data/', 'data/'];
32	
33	// Grandfathered: the pre-pipeline mock dataset the design-concepts prototypes
34	// still load, documented as such in README.md. It is not normalizer output and
35	// never will be; it is exempt by name so the rule can stay strict for everything
36	// else. Do not add to this list — new data comes from the normalizer.
37	const ALLOWED_FILES = new Set(['site/data/venues.json', 'data/shows.json']);
38	
39	// The one committed file under data/ that is an *input* to normalize.py rather
40	// than an output of it: the fetch-once ticket-price cache written by
41	// scraper/fetch_prices.py. It satisfies what this rule is actually protecting —
42	// a script in this repo produces it, and nothing silently destroys it (the
43	// normalizer only ever reads it) — so it is named here rather than exempted by
44	// shape. Anything else claiming to be a second input needs the same scrutiny
45	// this entry got, which is why it is one name and not a pattern.
46	const ALLOWED_INPUTS = new Map([
47	  ['data/prices.json', 'scraper/fetch_prices.py'],
48	]);
49	
50	// Committed files under data/ written by a generator in this repo that is NOT
51	// normalize.py. The site serves a second festival whose programme has its own
52	// one-shot scrape, and normalize.py neither writes nor reads that file — so it
53	// satisfies what this rule protects (a script in the repo produces it, and
54	// nothing silently destroys it) without being an input.
55	//
56	// Named, not shaped: a second festival's directory is exactly the moment a
57	// human should confirm the producer really writes what is in it, so a file that
58	// merely sits beside an allowed one still trips the rule.
59	const ALLOWED_OUTPUTS = new Map([
60	  ['site/data/jerusalem/shows.json', 'scraper/jerusalem/fetch.py'],
61	]);
62	
63	// The bulky raw scrape caches are git-ignored (`.gitignore`) precisely because
64	// each is regenerable by the scraper that fills it. One reaches the tree only
65	// via a deliberate `git add -f`, so it gets its own finding: the fix is to
66	// un-stage it, not to delete data the site needs.
67	const RAW_CACHES = new Map([
68	  ['data/raw_pages/', 'scraper/fetch_shows.py'],
69	  ['data/jerusalem/raw_pages/', 'scraper/jerusalem/fetch.py'],
70	]);
71	
72	const rule = {
73	  id: 'edfringe-data-dir-is-generator-output',
74	  severity: 'blocking',
75	  description: "Every committed file under site/data/ or data/ is one of scraper/normalize.py's outputs — no hand-made files, no probe dumps, no raw cache",
76	  why:
77	    'both data trees are generator output — site/data/ is fetched by the browser and the next refresh-shows run rewrites them wholesale, so a file that the normalizer does not produce is either silently served to users or silently destroyed — and either way the thing that produced it is not in the repo',
78	  doc: 'RULES.md',
79	
80	  run(ctx) {
81	    const out = [];
82	    for (const f of ctx.files.filter((p) => DATA_ROOTS.some((r) => p.startsWith(r))).sort()) {
83	      const cache = [...RAW_CACHES].find(([prefix]) => f.startsWith(prefix));
84	      if (cache) {
85	        out.push(finding(f,
86	          `${f} is a git-ignored raw scrape cache — un-track it (\`git rm --cached ${f}\`); ${cache[1]} regenerates it, so it is never committed`,
87	        ));
88	        continue;
89	      }
90	      if (ALLOWED_FILES.has(f) || ALLOWED_INPUTS.has(f) || ALLOWED_OUTPUTS.has(f)) continue;
91	      if (ALLOWED_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(f))) continue;
92	      out.push(finding(f,
93	        `delete ${f} — everything under site/data/ and data/ is scraper/normalize.py's output (site/data/venues.json, site/data/normalized/*.json, site/data/days/*.json, data/normalized/shows.json), plus the named scraper inputs (${[...ALLOWED_INPUTS.keys()].join(', ')}) and the named outputs of this repo's other generators (${[...ALLOWED_OUTPUTS.keys()].join(', ')}). A probe informs the normalizer, it does not feed it: fix scraper/normalize.py and re-run it instead. If normalize.py genuinely writes ${f} now, add its shape to this check's allowlist in the same commit; if another scraper in this repo produces it, add it to ALLOWED_INPUTS or ALLOWED_OUTPUTS naming that script`,
94	      ));
95	    }
96	    return out;
97	  },
98	};
99	
100	function finding(file, fix) {
101	  return {
102	    rule: rule.id,
103	    severity: rule.severity,
104	    file,
105	    line: null,
106	    what: `${file} is under a data tree but is not something a generator in this repo produces`,
107	    why: rule.why,
108	    fix,
109	    doc: rule.doc,
110	  };
111	}
112	
113	export default rule;

# by hand: `python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --recently-added ANY`.

          # Recovery RE-DERIVES rather than merges. Everything staged except

            python3 scraper/normalize.py --minify-from-master
          done

golden, a driven-gesture assertion, or a pure-rule test). The framework, its
lanes and the owner-approval contract live in
[product/requirements/README.md](product/requirements/README.md).

## Running

No build step. Because the app fetches `data/shows.json`, serve the folder over
HTTP rather than opening the file directly:

```
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

## Tech

- Plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript (no framework, no build tools)
- [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/) + OpenStreetMap tiles for the map (no API key)
- Mock show data in `data/shows.json`

## Structure

```
index.html        page markup
css/styles.css    styling
js/app.js         data loading, map, show list, journey, editable cards
js/places.js      non-show places: Nominatim geocoding + partner booking links
data/shows.json   mock Edinburgh Fringe shows
```

## Tests & CI

The planner's computation engine (`plan/lib/`) is unit-tested with the built-in
Node test runner — no dependencies, no install:

```
npm test          # node --test plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs
npm run verify     # tests + JS parse-checks (node --check) + Python py_compile
```

`npm run verify` is the single gate: it runs the unit tests, syntax-checks every
JavaScript source under `js/` and `plan/`, and byte-compiles the `scraper/`
Python. The release pipeline's PR gate (`.github/workflows/static-site-ci.yml`)

git branch --show-current && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Move the published site into site/

The cloudflare-site pack publishes exactly one directory — assets.directory in
a wrangler.json — and its publishes-a-site-directory check blocks pointing that
at the repo root, which here holds the vendored mount, the queue workers,
scraper/ and ~10 MB of pipeline inputs. Its release task has no build step: it
uploads the committed tree verbatim. So the published tree has to exist in the
repo as a directory before the host can change.

This is that reshape and nothing else. GitHub Pages still publishes, at the same
URLs: publish_root=site makes site/ the artifact's root, so "/" is still the Now
page and no fetch path in any page moves — every one of them was already
page-relative.

The split is now structural rather than a list of exclusions. data/ keeps the
pipeline's own working files (the master, the price cache, the raw caches);
site/data/ holds the wire files the browser fetches, so site.config can name
`data` as a plain directory where it used to enumerate six paths to hold back
the two 10 MB inputs. normalize.py names the two roots, and the workflows and
task workers that commit generated data stage both.

package.json cannot ride along: it is the repo's npm manifest at the root,
outside the published tree, and a tracked copy inside it would be a version free
to drift. The pages read site/version.json instead — the one fact they wanted out
of it — and both records are named in version_files, so the bump rewrites them
together and refuses outright unless they already agree.

Proved by the goldens: all 110 UI requirement cases pass pixel-identical, and the
served tree was driven in a real browser — all three pages fetch /version.json
and show v1.60916.1, with no application console errors.

Closes #730

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UaraYPNCgTxmYNDqNEk1sD
EOF

input.body:
Step 1 of the move off GitHub Pages onto Cloudflare. **Move only — GitHub Pages still publishes, at the same URLs.**

Closes #730

## Why this has to happen first

The `cloudflare-site` pack publishes exactly one directory — `assets.directory` in a `wrangler.json` — and its `publishes-a-site-directory` check *blocks* pointing that at the repo root, which here holds the vendored Claudinite mount, the queue workers, `scraper/` and ~10 MB of pipeline inputs. Its release task has **no build step**: it uploads the committed tree verbatim. So the published tree has to exist in the repo as a directory before the host can change at all.

Doing the reshape while still on Pages means it can be proved live before the host moves underneath it.

## What moved

`publish_root=site` makes `site/` the Pages artifact's *root*, so `/` is still the Now page and the live URLs gain no `/site/` prefix. Every fetch in the product was already page-relative, so **not one fetch path in any page changed**.

## The data split

`data/` now keeps only the pipeline's own working files — the master `data/normalized/shows.json`, `data/prices.json`, the git-ignored raw caches. `site/data/` holds the wire files the browser fetches.

That makes the publish boundary structural: `site.config` names `data` as a plain directory where it used to enumerate six paths specifically to hold back the two 10 MB scraper inputs. `normalize.py` names the two roots (`PIPELINE_DATA` / `SITE_DATA`), and the workflows and task workers that commit generated data stage both.

## The one thing that could not simply move

`package.json` is the repo's npm manifest at the root, outside the published tree — and the publish set must be tracked, so a generated copy is not an option either. A *tracked* copy inside `site/` would be a version number free to drift.

So the pages read **`site/version.json`** instead: the one fact they actually wanted out of `package.json`. Both records are named in `version_files`, so the bump rewrites them together — and it refuses outright unless every listed file already carries the same version, which is the drift guard rather than a second number to remember.

## How it was verified

- `npm run verify` — 289 tests, no blocking conformance findings.
- `npm run test:ui` — **all 110 UI requirement cases pass pixel-identical**. The pages' bytes did not move, so a golden that shifted would have meant the move broke something. None did.
- The publish set assembled exactly as the deploy builds it: `index.html` at the artifact root, 19 MB, with `plan/design/`, `data/prices.json` and the 7.4 MB master all absent.
- The served `site/` tree driven in a real headless Chromium: all three pages fetch `/version.json` → 200 and show the committed version, with no application console errors. The Now page renders its real show cards and the footer stamp reads `EdFringeNow v1.60916.1`; the planner loads its real catalogue ("Search all 4,122 shows").

## Not in this PR

No `wrangler.json`, no pack declaration change, no workflow deletions. Those are step 2, with the Cloudflare account steps (zone, nameservers, the two repository secrets) as step 3's handover issue — see #730 for the sequence.

entries.name: mcp__github__pull_request_read
entries.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.description: Update an existing pull request in a GitHub repository.

draft.description: Mark pull request as draft (true) or ready for review (false)

reviewers.description: GitHub usernames or ORG/team-slug team reviewers to request reviews from

Meanwhile, here's what the change touches:

```
site/            the whole published tree, moved here from the repo root — the four pages,
                 favicons, css/ js/ shared/ plan/ plan2/ planJerusalem/, plus site/data/ (the

scraper/         normalize.py now names the two roots explicitly (PIPELINE_DATA / SITE_DATA)

                 Jerusalem scrape splits its catalogue (published) from its page cache (not)

.github/         site.config takes publish_root=site, so the Pages artifact root IS the site

                 directory entry. scrape.yml and prices.yml stage both data trees

scripts/         build-site.sh stamps into site/js/; verify.sh syntax-checks 'site' in place of
                 the five old top-level source dirs

product/         the requirements harness serves from site/ rather than the repo root, the
                 fixture builder reads site/data/, and the version fixture became version.json

.claudinite/     the four local checks that hardcoded these paths, and the RULES.md prose that
                 names them, follow the move; the two refresh task workers stage both trees
```

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

{"total_count":2,"check_runs":[{"id":104827096922,"name":"ci","status":"completed","conclusion":"success","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/35105957281/job/104827096922","details_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/35105957281/job/104827096922","started_at":"2026-09-16T14:03:39Z","completed_at":"2026-09-16T14:04:01Z"},{"id":104827094903,"name":"ui-requirements","status":"in_progress","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/35105956858/job/104827094903","details_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/actions/runs/35105956858/job/104827094903","started_at":"2026-09-16T14:03:39Z"}]}

`ci` is green and the assemble dry-run proved the new publish set. `ui-requirements` (110 real-browser golden comparisons) is still running; I'll report when it lands.

**What I did**

You asked to adopt the relevant pack and go. I found `cloudflare-site` in the canon and read it end to end before touching anything — and it forced one thing worth knowing early: it publishes exactly *one* directory, its release task has **no build step** (it uploads the committed tree verbatim), and a check blocks pointing that at a repo root. Your call was to land the reshape on its own, still on Pages. That's [PR #731](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/731), closing [#730](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/730).

Two things I decided rather than asked:

- **`package.json` couldn't come along.** It's npm's manifest at the root, outside the published tree; the publish set must be *tracked*, so a generated copy was out too, and a tracked copy inside `site/` is a version free to drift. The pages now read a tiny `site/version.json` — the one fact they wanted from it — and both records sit in `version_files`, so the bump rewrites them together and *refuses* unless they already agree. That's the drift guard, built into the tool rather than remembered.
- **Docs followed the move**, including the local pack's `RULES.md` (it loads into every session, so stale paths there actively mislead) — carefully, since several `shared/` references in it are the requirements harness's, not the site's.

One thing I checked rather than assumed: the `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` warning that appeared during testing. It fires on `main` too — pre-existing, not a regression from the move, so I left it.

**Ahead of us**, once this is merged and you've seen the live site: step 2 is the actual Cloudflare swap (declare `cloudflare-site`, undeclare `static-website`, `wrangler.json`, retire the five `static-site-*` workflows). One gap I'll flag now rather than at the time — **no canon pack owns generic CI**, so dropping `static-website` drops the PR gate with it and the repo will need its own `ci.yml`. Step 3 is yours: the zone, the nameserver move, and the two repository secrets.

> ⚠️ Still open: `ui-requirements` in flight on [#731](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/731) — locally all 110 goldens passed pixel-identical, so I expect green. Steps 2 and 3 of the migration are not started, by your sequencing.
